tob-10066: Christian Ginsburg’s nineteenth-century study introduces Kabbalah, the mystical tradition within Judaism, to English readers. tob-10466: The second volume of John Calvin’s Institutes completes his system of Reformed doctrine, covering the church, the sacraments, and the Christian life. Here Calvin sets out his famous teaching on predestination alongside practical guidance for prayer, obedience, and civic duty. Together the two volumes became the charter of Presbyterian and Reformed churches worldwide.
tob-0166: Bahá’u’lláh, founder of the Bahá’í faith, wrote the Seven Valleys as a chart of the soul’s road to God — through vales of seeking, love, knowing, oneness, content, wonder, and true poverty. tob-12966: James Legge’s Chinese Classics string the heart-books of Confucian teaching — Analects, Great Learning, Mean, Mencius — with the old text and full scholar’s gear. His decades of toil made him the West’s great China-reader. The set stays the groundwork of English Confucian study.
tob-4066: Max Muller’s Rig-Veda is the trail-blazing English of Hinduism’s oldest writ — a thousand and twenty-eight hymns to sky, fire, and storm gods, sung above three thousand years ago. His decades of toil grounded Veda-learning in the West. The volumes stay monuments of Victorian scholarship.
tob-10266: Lévi’s Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie — 1854-56 — is the founding text of modern occultism, in its original French. tob-4166: Andrew Lang’s Myth, Ritual, and Religion — 1887 — argues that myths arose from savage custom and ritual, not from language. The great folklorist’s work challenged Max Müller’s solar theory. The debate shaped the field. The book is a classic of early anthropology.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ClarkRamseyExec: Ramsey Clark’s Providing for the Acquisition and Preservation of Evidence — the 1966 executive order — is a legal file. The order protected the JFK evidence. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of the legal record.

arxiv-2606-17366: Aurelie Kemme, Collins Agyingi, and Colleen Farratt extract a persistent homology signature of knotting. arxiv-2606-18066: The NoiseTilt paper introduces noise-tilted reverse kernels for diffusion reward alignment. Tilting the noise steers generation toward rewarded outcomes. arxiv-2606-18166: Ahmed Ryan and colleagues evaluate open-source LLMs for multi-label ATT&CK technique classification on cyber threat reports. arxiv-2606-18266: Nelly Garcia and colleagues examine how audio parameters shape emotional responses and immersion in film with EMORSION. arxiv-2606-18366: Mårten Schultzberg derives a closed-form sample size correction for always-valid inference with optional stopping. plos-pone-0003466: Physiologists found men's and women's muscles hear hunger signals differently in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003566: Psychologists found music lessons tuning young minds in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003666: In 2008, a team showed faces swaying votes by gender. Voters judged the faces of those running, and those snap reads predicted voting, but the reads tilted by the runner's gender. The work exposes a facial bias: how a leader looks moves ballots differently for men and women.
plos-pone-0003766: Vogt, D'Angelo, and Oswald pulled a light switch from the deep sea in this 2008 paper. Their new green fluorescent protein, found in a deep-sea creature, can be switched on and off with light. The photoswitchable marker gives cell biologists a sharper tool for live imaging.
plos-pone-0003866: In 2008, a team compared fast-aging fish strains. The short-lived annual killifish Nothobranchius furzeri showed large aging differences between strains. The strain comparison turns this tiny fish into a powerful model for studying why we age.
plos-pone-0003966: In 2008, Tan, Schedl, and Song linked an immune pathway to Alzheimer's damage in flies. Toll-to-NF-kB signaling mediated the harmful effects of the human amyloid-beta 42 peptide. The fly model implicates innate immunity in neurodegeneration.
plos-pone-0004066: In 2008, Mine, Fortunel, and Pageon found skin aging is layer-deep. Aging altered the function of papillary dermal fibroblasts. plos-pone-0004166: In 2009, Courtney, Ofek, and Penfound linked germ slipperiness to stickiness. M protein and lipoteichoic acid levels set how germs shun water. The surface traits fed sticking and biofilm growth in strep germs. The neat link exposes targets for future anti-stick drugs.
plos-pone-0004366: In 2009, Gingerich, ul-Haq, and von Koenigswald found a whale born on land. A new protocetid whale from Pakistan's middle Eocene showed land birth and precocial young. The four-legged predator predated true whales by millions of years. The fossil bridges land and sea beautifully.
plos-pone-0004466: In 2009, Sone, Uchida, and Komatsu found a gene guiding protein delivery. Loss of yata, a novel gene, mislocalized APPL and harmed young fly brains. The delivery gene's absence scrambled transport. The finding maps neural trafficking routes. The flies slowly deteriorated.
plos-pone-0004566: In 2009, Prabakaran, Ho, and Prabhu built a universal bird-flu antibody test kit. An epitope-blocking ELISA universally detected antibodies to human H5N1 influenza. The blood test beat slow culture methods. The tool aids global surveillance. The target flu is H5N1.
plos-pone-0004666: In 2009, Dinkla, Talay, and Mörgelin pinned a heart-disease trigger on collagen. The crucial role of collagen IV's CB3 region in PARF-induced acute rheumatic fever was shown. The bacterial protein targeted heart collagen. The finding maps autoimmunity. The sequelae are serious.
plos-pone-0004766: In 2009, a team probed a kinase's taste in targets anew here. The CKIε kinase met two targets from far-apart signal paths. The kinase showed clear favorites indeed. The study maps cell signal wiring today. The family forms are seven total.
plos-pone-0358966: Lectures, bedside teaching, group work — medical students at Nigeria’s Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University were asked which teaching methods they actually prefer. plos-pone-0358066: People living with HIV face higher cancer risks, but the pattern in Uganda was poorly mapped. plos-pone-0358566: Gun violence in the West Bank leaves a trail of injuries that few studies have documented. The data give health planners and trauma teams the first solid picture of who gets shot, how badly, and what saves them.
plos-pone-0358366: Not knowing what your cancer will do next is its own torment. This paper used latent profile analysis to map illness uncertainty in women with gynecologic and breast cancer. The distinct uncertainty profiles point to which patients need the most support navigating the unknown.
plos-pone-0357466: What do kids actually think of natural history museums? This paper captured children’s perceptions through Portugal’s ‘Young Naturalists’ program. plos-pone-0356366: Locking up petty offenders might manufacture more criminals, not fewer. The numbers put a measurable price on the school-of-crime effect that reformers have long warned about.
plos-pone-0346466: Spotty liver disease costs the egg industry millions in lost production. This paper mapped the hepatic transcriptomic landscape of chickens to reveal host responses to the disease. plos-pone-0358266: Babies born with duct-dependent lung circulation need a lifeline: a ductal stent or a Blalock–Taussig shunt. The head-to-head results guide heart surgeons choosing the safer bridge to definitive repair in these fragile newborns.
plos-pone-0358466: Cancer treatment can steal fertility — but many survivors still become mothers against the odds. This Taiwanese population-based study measured rates of childbirth in female cancer survivors. The rates give survivors realistic hope and give doctors solid data for honest fertility counseling.
plos-pone-0357966: Chronic low oxygen rewires the heart and scrambles its internal clock. The split responses reveal how hearts cope with thin air — adapting in some systems while faltering in others.
plos-pone-0356266: Passion fruit viruses threaten harvests across the tropics — and early detection is everything. The test hands growers a fast, reliable way to catch infection before it spreads.
plos-pone-0357666: Esports for seniors sounds like a joke — but the results are serious. The feasibility results open a surprising door to keeping aging minds and bodies active.
plos-pone-0356566: Measuring leg strength accurately on the leg press demands the right loading strategy. This paper identified the optimal two-point loading strategy for accurate leg press force–velocity assessment. The validated protocol gives sports scientists trustworthy strength profiles.
plos-pone-0355466: Natural product drug screening is plagued by false alarms from pan-assay interference compounds. This paper proposed a bioactivity-leveling approach for component-specific evaluation, optimizing SARS-CoV-2 antiviral screening by controlling for those nuisance compounds. The method separates genuine antiviral hits from chemical noise.
plos-pone-0356766: South Korea’s AI ethical principles needed a refresh after five fast-moving years. This paper supplemented the original principles with a five-year update. The revised framework grapples with generative AI and other developments the first version never imagined.
plos-pone-0354366: Dentists see smokers regularly — a missed opportunity for cessation counseling. This cross-sectional study captured views from patients and dentists as key stakeholders on smoking cessation counseling in primary dental care. The dual perspectives reveal why the dental chair remains an underused front in the fight against tobacco.
plos-pone-0355866: Cities drown in stormwater — but compost-amended soil can drink it up. This paper showed compost incorporation improves infiltration rates and associated soil hydro-physical properties as a stormwater management intervention. The humble amendment turns compacted urban ground into a sponge — a cheap, green defense against flooding.
plos-pone-0354966: Choosing how many components a model needs — and how much to shrink them — is usually guesswork. plos-pone-0347366: Gene regulation evolves — but do regulatory connections survive across species? plos-pone-0355166: Measuring tobacco smoke exposure in Saudi women — where smoking is stigmatized — needs objective biomarkers. This paper assessed exposure via urinary cotinine analysis. plos-pone-0356066: Screening for adverse childhood experiences — in clinic versus by phone — yields different answers. This paper compared ACEs reporting between clinic and telephone-based screening. plos-pone-0354466: Detecting objects through bad weather — rain, fog, darkness — needs RGB fused with thermal vision. plos-pone-0353666: Female reproductive history — pregnancies, menopause — may influence eye pressure and glaucoma risk. plos-pone-0344266: Detecting events — from news, sensors, social media — demands fusing multiple sources and modalities. This paper used graph convolutional networks for multi-source multimodal event detection. The graph-based fusion spots the happenings that single-source systems miss.
plos-pone-0353166: Vietnamese administrative documents — dense with named entities — needed a recognition corpus. PAP_NER provides it: a large-scale Vietnamese administrative NER corpus with a hybrid deep learning architecture. The resource brings Vietnamese bureaucratic text into the NLP age.
plos-pone-0354666: Pregnant women in Garowe, Somalia — anemia and its factors. This antenatal care study documented them. The findings give Puntland’s health system the risk factors to target — because anemic mothers bear vulnerable babies.
plos-pone-0353266: U.S. healthcare professionals’ RSV knowledge, attitudes, and practices — during the 2024–2025 season. This paper surveyed them for adult disease and vaccination. plos-pone-0327266: Kenyan men’s non-communicable diseases — prevalence and factors from 2022 demographic and health survey data. This cross-sectional analysis did so. plos-pone-0354266: High-volatile bituminous coal — its molecular structure — constructed via multi-technique characterization. This paper did so. plos-pone-0353866: Corneal inflammation — LPS-induced in mice — alleviated by the PAC1 receptor agonist maxadilan. This paper demonstrated it. plos-pone-0353766: COVID-19’s excess mortality — analyzed by age across selected countries. This paper did so. The age-stratified analysis revealed the pandemic’s wildly uneven toll. The findings quantified what demographics already suggested — age as the master variable of COVID-19 mortality.
plos-pone-0353966: Andean soil organic carbon — predicted better with crop rotation history integrated via machine learning. This paper asked whether rotation history improves predictions. plos-pone-0352966: Folic acid knowledge and attitudes — cross-culturally assessed in Thailand and Yemen. This paper developed and validated the instrument. plos-pone-0352166: Rohu fish gene knockout — mstnb — donor DNA designed and validated in silico for RNA-guided recombinase editing. This paper did so in Labeo rohita. The findings enabled precision breeding of a vital food fish. The research served aquaculture — genetics for the dinner table.
plos-pone-0353466: Image captions — contextual — created with object positional embedding and generative models. This paper built it. The findings taught AI where things are, not just what they are. The research advanced the vision-language — captions that understand the scene’s geography.
plos-pone-0350166: Human-elephant conflict near Kruger National Park — causes revealed, social media narratives unpicked. This paper did both. The findings separated real drivers from viral stories. plos-pone-0341766: Oral disease registry — large-scale — established at a national specialty center. The NDCS-ODR is that registry. The paper described its creation. plos-pone-0352866: Diurnal temperature range — a climatological primer for health researchers. This paper wrote it. The findings explained the daily thermal swing’s health relevance. plos-pone-0350666: Time series missing data — imputed via significant periodically correlated components. This paper built the strategies. The findings filled the gaps using the series’ own rhythms. plos-pone-0352766: Contracts law keyword list — CLKL developed for academic legal education via corpus keyness. This paper built it. The findings gave law teachers the vocabulary. plos-pone-0346766: Ghana’s Volta River — downstream community risks after dam-spillage flooding, with potential pathogens and public health implications. This paper assessed them. plos-pone-0351966: Financial tail risk networks — dynamic, via a backtesting-based conditional expected shortfall approach. This paper built them. plos-pone-0349666: Apolipoprotein C3 — stage-dependent dynamics across the MASLD spectrum. This paper tracked them. The analysis followed the protein through fatty liver stages. europmc-pmc2814866: Fat tissue is not just storage, it is active biology, and this 2010 paper profiles its microRNA regulators. europmc-pmc2815666: A companion to the XDS paper, this 2010 article by Wolfgang Kabsch covers the next steps in crystallography data processing. europmc-pmc2831066: The amyloid beta protein blamed in Alzheimer's may have a day job fighting germs. This 2010 paper reports that it acts as an antimicrobial peptide, killing microbes in lab tests. europmc-pmc2851566: One DNA patch, 9p21, kept turning up in diseases from heart trouble to tumors. This 2010 paper ties its SNPs to many disease forms and links them to ANRIL, a nearby RNA. The team bared a shared root. The find hinted one patch may steer several diseases.
europmc-pmc2897766: Cells tune their stress response with exquisite care. This 2010 paper shows BiP binding to the stress sensor Ire1 tunes the unfolded protein response's homeostatic behavior. europmc-pmc2911766: Surgery patients do better when fluids are tuned, not poured. This 2010 randomized study tests fluid tuning with stroke volume variation in high-risk surgery patients. The authors show guided fluids beat fixed doses. Their result changed how anesthesia teams handle fluids.
europmc-pmc3013466: Disgust evolved to keep us from disease. This 2011 paper argues the yuck response is a disease-avoidance system. The authors make the evolutionary case. Their work reframed a basic emotion. Rotten smells trigger the ancient alarm. Moral disgust may borrow the same wiring.
europmc-pmc3111466: Wheat fiber fed good gut bugs in fat mice. This 2011 paper shows wheat arabinoxylan boosts bifidobacteria and friends in obese mice. The authors link fiber to flora. Their work backs prebiotics. Weight gain slowed on the fiber diet. Whole grains may work the same way.

europmc-pmc3156766: Africa's diabetes surge got mapped. This 2011 review tracks diabetes across sub-Saharan Africa from 1999 to 2011. The authors reveal the steep rise. europmc-pmc3267166: A tumor-starving drug got a design review. This 2010 paper traces cilengitide's design, synthesis, and trials. The authors map the path. Their overview guides pharma. The drug starved tumors of blood. Trials tested it in brain cancer. Kessler's lab led the work.
europmc-pmc3314666: A flu shot got a narcolepsy link. This 2012 paper links Finland's H1N1 vaccine to a spike in childhood narcolepsy. The authors reveal the increase. Their work shaped vaccine safety. Risk rose twelvefold, they found. Nohynek's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3384466: Adult disease got a womb origin. This 2012 paper reviews how womb conditions shape adult disease. The authors map the origins. Their overview guides policy. Barouki's review is widely cited. It is a classic. It shaped prenatal policy. The DOHaD field grew from it.
europmc-pmc6522366: Two mosquitoes - Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus - carry dengue, Zika, yellow fever, and chikungunya, and their territory keeps growing. europmc-pmc6548966: Growing a replacement heart patch - thick, with its own blood vessels, matched to the patient - has been a pipe dream. europmc-pmc6558766: One in six American mothers in a landmark survey reported mistreatment during pregnancy or childbirth - being shouted at, ignored, or pressured into procedures. europmc-pmc6567666: A genome-scale metabolic model is a digital twin of a cell's chemistry - every gene linked to the reactions it drives. europmc-pmc6626766: Designer nanoparticles promise to outsmart cancer's defenses: homing to tumors, slipping past barriers, and releasing drugs on cue. europmc-pmc6627766: Eating all your meals early - time-restricted feeding - may steady blood sugar around the clock. europmc-pmc6647366: Solid tumors outgrow their blood supply, turning acidic and oxygen-starved - conditions where carbonic anhydrase IX thrives. europmc-pmc6670166: New to systematic reviews? This step-by-step guide walks beginners through one using simulated data - from question to search to analysis.
